tasks.short: Review an account and determine whether to propose a collection-agency write-off.

steps.what: Assemble the account balance, payment history, contact attempts, dispute status, collateral notes and prior collection actions
Check recoverability, active disputes and the collection history, then record a reasoned write-off recommendation or retention decision
Route the recommendation and the frozen evidence list to the collections manager for a separate write-off decision
Correct missing records or explain the recommendation to the collections manager when the review is returned

tasks.design: A {CRM} review dossier puts the payment and collection evidence in one place. The officer makes a documented recoverability judgement; a separate manager decides any write-off.
tasks.previous_blocker: The officer searches ledgers, notes and attachments before applying collection policy.
tasks.enabler_now: Account and collection events can be assembled against one case identifier.
tasks.still_hard: Recoverability, disputes and the appropriateness of a write-off are accountable financial judgements.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can recognise a disputed balance or a fact that makes the collection history unreliable.

ambition.what: Compare returned recommendations to improve the completeness of future write-off reviews.

tasks.altitude: The officer concentrates on the evidence and exceptions behind a consequential collection recommendation.

evidence.claim: A case view can assemble internal account and collection records into a review dossier.

assumptions: The boundary ends at a manager-review task, not an approved write-off or agency transfer.
The dossier lists the source and timestamp for each balance and collection event.
An active dispute always remains for manual review.
One hour per 100 focal-role baseline hours is allowed for dossier field and policy-rule maintenance.
unknowns: Which fields managers most often find missing from current write-off reviews.
research_questions: What share of reviews are returned because evidence is incomplete?

incremental.description: Maintain dossier fields and policy mapping

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Evidence assembly and routing are automated; judgement and returned-review work remain, with upkeep deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review billing records for accuracy before they are relied on.

steps.what: Ingest the billing record, account terms, payment postings and any charge or fee adjustments for the review period
Compare billed amounts, dates and fee codes against the account terms and payment events, and flag a discrepancy with its source rows

loop.input: billing lines, payment events and applicable fee rules
loop.check: the system checks account ID, billing period, amount, date and fee code against the available rules
loop.stop: stop automatic matching when a source row or applicable term is missing; place the record in the discrepancy queue
loop.why_not_simpler: The comparison is structured but different products and adjustments require the applicable account terms.

steps.what: Investigate each discrepancy by reading the contract, adjustment evidence and transaction history, then record whether the billing is correct or needs correction
Create an internal correction task with the reviewed billing line and supporting evidence for the billing team

tasks.design: A {DATA_PLATFORM} comparison flags source-linked mismatches. The officer investigates exceptions and the workflow creates an internal correction task; it does not alter a bill.
tasks.previous_blocker: The officer manually aligns billed lines, terms and payment records before identifying the few that need investigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Billing, payment and account-term fields can be compared with stable matching keys.
tasks.still_hard: A fee adjustment or contract exception can only be judged by reading its supporting evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can distinguish a true billing mistake from an authorised adjustment.

ambition.what: Use mismatch reasons to improve billing controls and reduce recurring exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The officer reviews evidence-rich exceptions instead of checking every billing line by hand.

evidence.claim: Structured billing and transaction fields can be compared to produce source-linked internal exceptions.

assumptions: The boundary ends with an internal correction task, not a changed or issued bill.
The comparison retains source record IDs, account terms version and matching result.
Missing terms and unmatched adjustments are always reviewed by a person.
Two hours per 100 focal-role baseline hours are allowed for rule monitoring and exception taxonomy maintenance.
unknowns: How many billing differences arise from authorised manual adjustments.
research_questions: What percentage of flagged lines are confirmed billing errors?

incremental.description: Maintain comparison rules and mismatch taxonomy

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Data intake, comparison and internal task creation are automated; exception investigation remains and upkeep is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Improve the quality of lending operations by working on evidence gaps, recurring exceptions and clear client records.
role.ambitious_version: Make high-consequence lending records accurate and explainable before downstream decisions are made.
